subject: Data lifecycle / TTL clarifications for DPA and SIG

Cc: AcmeHealth Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-21 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Data lifecycle / TTL clarifications for DPA and SIG

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our procurement and SIG review we need a concise data-lifecycle summary to attach to the DPA. Specifically we need answers (and evidence where possible) for the following items: 

- Primary request/transaction logs: retention period, whether logs contain prompt text or only metadata, encryption at rest, and deletion workflow.
- Backups/snapshots: frequency, retention TTL, whether backups include any prompt or user-submitted text, and the restore-window policy.
- Prompt retention / cache: do you persist prompts beyond the immediate inference for debugging or quality, and if so what's the TTL and opt-out mechanism?
- KV cache and model-derived artifacts: whether these are stored persistently and how they are purged.
- SLA / contractual deletion timeline after contract termination or data subject request (DPA/erasure): what is the maximum window and evidence you provide (audit logs, certificate, or export).

We'd appreciate a short matrix and any supporting artifacts (SOC 2 or SIG evidence, screenshots of audit logs, or a redlined DPA clause). Can you get this to me within 3 business days?

Best,
Sofia Ruiz
Data Protection Officer
AcmeHealth

Attachment: sigs-request.pdf (requested questionnaire)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ruiz <sofia.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, AcmeHealth Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-21 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle / TTL clarifications for DPA and SIG

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear list. Putting a short matrix together and attaching a vendor-friendly summary. High level answers below; I'll follow up with the detailed matrix and supporting artifacts by tomorrow.

- Request/transaction logs: Default retention 90 days for full request logs (includes prompt text by default for debugging and evals), metadata-only retention available via config. Logs are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and our managed KMS for Hosted. Deletion: automated lifecycle job marks logs for deletion and purges within 14 days of TTL expiry; deletion operations are captured in an audit trail.
- Backups/snapshots: Nightly snapshots, retained for 180 days by default. Snapshots do include persisted inputs if the customer has opted-in to prompt retention; for customers requiring zero prompt persistence in backups we can apply an exclude filter at snapshot time (Private and Dedicated customers only).
- Prompt retention / cache: By default, prompt text is persisted for 30 days for troubleshooting and model-quality monitoring. We offer an opt-out to set prompt retention to 0 days (ephemeral-only) at contract start or via an account setting for Dedicated/Private.
- KV cache and derived artifacts: KV caches are in-memory per runtime and persisted only to short-lived local caches for warm-starting (TTL: 1 hour). Any derived embeddings or artifacts that are stored have explicit TTLs configurable per account.
- Erasure / contract termination: Standard DPA erasure window is 45 days post-termination to complete exports and deletions; emergency deletions (customer-initiated) can be expedited with signed request and an SLA to 7 days plus deletion audit evidence.

I'll attach: data-lifecycle-matrix.csv (detailed per-item TTLs), and a proposed DPA clause redline for AcmeHealth to review. Ben, Grace — flag anything inaccurate or add notes about SOC 2 / audit evidence we can ship.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: data-lifecycle-matrix.csv, proposed-dpa-clause-redline.docx

On Wed, 21 Mar 2028 at 10:03, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> - Request/transaction logs: Default retention 90 days for full request logs (includes prompt text by default for debugging and evals), metadata-only retention available via config. Logs are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and our managed KMS for Hosted. Deletion: automated lifecycle job marks logs for deletion and purges within 14 days of TTL expiry; deletion operations are captured in an audit trail.

Adding some technical detail for your SIG reviewers:
- Audit evidence: for SOC 2 / SIG we can provide redacted samples of audit-log exports that show deletion events (timestamps, object ids) and an architecture diagram showing lifecycle jobs. For customers under NDA we provide a read-only export of deletion events via S3 link (signed URL).
- Backups: snapshots are incremental; full content is encrypted and stored in a separate storage tier. For PHI/HIPAA customers we recommend enabling snapshot-exclude for prompts and using a dedicated backup vault (customer encrypted) — this is standard in our Dedicated/Private offering.
- Prompt opt-out: enabling prompt opt-out toggles both live retention and snapshot inclusion via a pre-snapshot scrubbing step. We capture opt-out toggles in the audit trail so you have proof the setting was active at a given time.

I'll attach a one-page SOC 2 evidence checklist and a sample redacted deletion log to the Drive link Markus shared. Grace — can you confirm the export path and whether we can supply the deletion export as a signed S3 link for Acme?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Can you confirm you can sign a DPA with that clause?
